newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Hilton Hotels ups debt offer.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Hilton Hotels ups debt offer.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp said Tuesday it was increasing its offer to certain debt holders of Bally Entertainment Corp and its units in connection with its pending merger.
A copy of the company's news release follows.

BEVERLY HILLS, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 19, 1996--Hilton Hotels Corp. (NYSE:HLT) Tuesday announced that it is increasing the consideration being offered to the holders of certain issues of notes of Bally Entertainment Corp.'s (NYSE:BLY) wholly owned subsidiaries in connection with the pending offer to purchase and consent solicitation for such notes.

The offers are part of the refinancing related to Hilton's pending merger with Bally and are contingent upon, among other things, closing of the merger. The completion of the merger is not contingent upon the close of the tender offers.

Upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the offer to purchase and the letter of transmittal previously distributed to holders, Hilton is now offering to purchase for cash any and all of the following issues at the following increased purchase prices:

-- 9-1/4 percent Bally's Park Place Funding Inc. First Mortgage Notes due March 2004 ($425 million outstanding at Sept. 30, 1996) for 110.21 percent (based on a spread of 50 basis points over the corresponding Treasury at 2 p.m. ET on Nov. 18, and composed of 108.21 percent for the tender consideration and 2.00 percent for the consent fee) of their principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest to the date of purchase;

-- 10-5/8 percent GNF Corp. First Mortgage Notes due April 2003 ($275 million outstanding at Sept. 30, 1996) for 110.55 percent (based on a spread of 50 basis points over the corresponding Treasury at 2 p.m. ET on Nov. 18, and composed of 108.55 percent for the tender consideration and 2.00 percent for the consent fee) of their principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest to the date of purchase;

-- Bally's Casino Holdings Inc. senior discount notes and senior discount notes due June 1998 ($96.1 million of accreted value at Sept. 30, 1996, excluding $69.8 million accreted value of such notes that are owned by Bally) for 106.64 percent (based on a spread of 50 basis points over the corresponding Treasury at 2 p.m. ET on Nov. 18, and composed of 104.64 percent for the tender consideration and 2.00 percent for the consent fee) of their accreted value to the date of purchase.

Hilton also announced Tuesday that it is increasing the consideration being offered to the holders of the 10-3/8 percent First Mortgage Notes due December 2003 of Bally's Grand Inc. (NYSE:BGLV), an 85 percent-owned subsidiary of Bally, in connection with the pending offer to purchase and consent solicitation for such notes.

The offer is part of the refinancing related to Hilton's pending merger with Bally and is contingent upon, among other things, closing of the merger. The completion of the merger is not contingent upon the close of the tender offer.

Upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the offer to purchase and the letter of transmittal previously distributed to holders, Hilton is now offering to purchase for cash any and all of the 10-3/8 percent Bally's Grand First Mortgage Notes due December 2003 ($315 million outstanding at Sept. 30, 1996) for 112.39 percent (based on a spread of 50 basis points over the corresponding Treasury at 2 p.m. ET on Nov. 18, and composed of 110.39 percent for the tender consideration and 2.00 percent for the consent fee) of their principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest to the date of purchase.

The consent date for each series of notes will occur at 5 p.m. ET on the later of (i) the fifth business day immediately preceding the expiration of the tender offer or (ii) the date the respective supplemental indenture with respect to such notes is executed. Holders who tender notes in the offers will be deemed to consent to the proposed amendments to the indentures governing the notes.
Holders may not deliver a consent to the proposed amendments without also tendering their related notes.
Holders must consent to the proposed amendments to the indentures and tender their notes prior to the consent date in order to receive both the consent fee and the tender considerations.
All of the tender offers will expire at 9:30 a.m. ET on Thursday, Dec. 12, unless extended by Hilton. Based on this expiration date, the consent date is expected to be Thursday, Dec. 5.

This announcement is neither an offer to purchase nor a solicitation of an offer to purchase any series of notes. The offers to purchase and consent solicitations are being made solely by the offers to purchase and consent solicitations dated Oct. 25, 1996, as supplemental, and the increased consideration being offered to all holders remains subject to all terms and conditions stated therein.

Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp.; Bear, Stearns & Co. Inc.; and Goldman, Sachs & Co. are acting as dealer managers. MacKenzie Partners Inc. is acting as the information agent for the tender offers and consent solicitations.
